# Public authorization fixtures

Synthetic example-domain URLs, client identifiers and provider responses are authored under the repository license. No real accounts, secrets or package content are used. `t27_tests.rs` covers S256/state, callback validation and URL question handling. `t27_flow_tests.rs` installs a real temporary plugin, uses its source-bound MCP declaration and the real question store, opens a real loopback browser callback and sends real HTTP provider requests. Only metadata/provider addresses and user answers are substituted at explicit boundaries. Success proves verifier/challenge, resource/client/redirect binding and unchanged original package bytes; denial, cancellation, timeout, forged state/issuer and source changes prevent token exchange and close listeners/questions. DCR and operator-configured CIMD cover public client registration; explicit empty scopes remain empty. `server.py` is a real stdio MCP peer that receives and echoes the exact URL elicitation response ID.

Frozen reference symbols: `codex-mcp/src/mcp/auth.rs::{resolve_oauth_callback,resolve_oauth_scopes}`, `rmcp-client/src/oauth_client_registration.rs::start_authorization`, and `codex-mcp/src/elicitation.rs::{ElicitationRequestRouter,request_user_interaction,ResponderMap}`. Their SHA-256 values match the existing read-only baseline. URL completion is a server/request-bound user response; the reviewed frozen runtime has no `elicitation/complete` notification path. No Codex-hosted identity endpoint is copied. Public-provider/browser and actual desktop rendering acceptance remain user-deferred external evidence.
